checks.detail: The core verifies an Ed25519 signature over canonical payload JSON. A changed gate fails verification.
The block reads integrity and freshness from PassHost. Model-supplied trust fields are ignored.
Snapshot metadata is HMAC-sealed with a non-extractable WebCrypto key. Tampering fails validation.
A new offline host restored the verified snapshot in a real browser and marked freshness stale.
A slow issuer response timed out and the host fell back to the sealed snapshot. The hosted smoke recorded exactly one /pass request and no automatic retry.
A revoked feed produced integrity=revoked, disabled the QR, and preserved revoked through the snapshot.
A tampered feed signature produced integrity=invalid and no verified badge.
Malformed flight, seat, route, and QR props drop the pass op with an invalid_pass issue.
DSH declares canVerifyPass=true and read-only show_code, refresh, request_verification, and open_issuer_link. canOpenWallet remains false.

The pass block reports host attestation to the compiler. A stale/unknown/unverified/invalid/revoked pass inserts a visible conclusion warning and data-iui-freshness; a live pass removes it. Model prose is not rewritten.

Refresh/request_verification run through ActionRuntime. A timed-out refresh records timeout, enters reconciliation, records a failed reconciliation with timeout/snapshot evidence, and makes exactly one host call.

clear() bumps a UI epoch, invalidates in-flight generations, clears memory immediately, deletes IndexedDB records and the HMAC key, and clears again after in-flight tasks settle. DSH listens to account-ui/change with a signed-out view and to session/disposed; plugin unload also clears. On 2026-11-19 an isolated hosted DSH 0.2.2-rc.3 profile performed a real account UI sign-out: the mounted pass block entered the pass-cleared state, IndexedDB snapshots/meta went 1/2 -> 0/0, and the account became signed out. Remote provider revocation was suppressed by a test-only patch in the disposable runtime so the real token was not consumed. Restoring the same credential signed the account in again; the pass reloaded verified/live and wrote only a fresh snapshot. The block remained mounted as a cleared notice; the earlier temporary-emitter event-path run cleared 8 mounted blocks.

URL QR payloads and open_issuer_link require an exact https origin from host config or the configured https issuer origin. Opaque IUI1 payloads remain allowed. No allowlist means URL payloads are rejected.

DSH 0.2.2-rc.3 with DeepSeek Account and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash rendered the test-issuer pass. Playwright exercised QR show-code, stale snapshot plus conclusion warning, revoked (QR disabled), invalid, slow timeout with one request, recovery to live, and cleared conclusion warnings. Console errors: 0. This used the local test issuer, not a real airline.

2026-11-19 follow-up: a real hosted account UI sign-out in an isolated DSH 0.2.2-rc.3 profile. The pass block showed "Pass data was cleared on sign-out", IndexedDB snapshots/meta went 1/2 -> 0/0, and console errors were 0. The remote provider revocation call was suppressed by a test-only patch in the disposable runtime; the real account token was not consumed. After restoring the same credential, the account signed in and the pass reloaded verified/live from the test issuer with a new snapshot only. A fresh device authorization and hosted session/disposed were not exercised.

notProven: A real airline, hotel, rail, Google Wallet, or Apple Wallet issuer.
Real-world credential validity or airport scanner compatibility.

Remote provider-side revocation and a fresh device authorization after the C30 fix. The 2026-11-19 hosted UI sign-out used a test-only patch to suppress remote revocation so the real token stayed valid; re-login restored the same credential in the isolated profile.
Hosted session/disposed cleanup. The current DSH Web UI does not emit this event on archive or normal navigation, so the listener and local tests cover it but a hosted disposal was not produced.
A real issuer-domain allowlist or production allowlist rotation process.
caveats: The test issuer generates a fresh key pair on each process start. This is not production key management.
The browser tests use the local test issuer and a synthetic boarding pass. They do not use passenger data from a real booking.

C30 now clears on the hosted account sign-out event and keeps session disposal as a second boundary. The 2026-11-19 real UI sign-out used an isolated profile and a test-only remote-revocation suppression; the pass block entered the cleared state, IndexedDB snapshots/meta went 1/2 -> 0/0, and a credential-restored re-login produced only a fresh verified/live snapshot. Remote provider revocation and fresh device authorization were not exercised.
The test-only revocation-suppression patch existed only in the disposable DSH runtime under the temporary directory. It is not part of this repository, and it was removed with that runtime.
The slow-refresh hosted smoke observed one /pass request and no automatic retry. Its wall-clock observation included UI polling; it is not a latency benchmark.
The historical tool rows can keep the inline timeout message after a later pass recovers. The latest pass recovered to live and the conclusion warning was removed.

npm audit --audit-level=low currently reports 4 high-severity build-tool findings in picomatch through Vite. No dependency upgrade is included in this follow-up. The rc.3 dependency update was clean when it was recorded.
No API key, route token, session record, screenshot, private key, or real credential is included in this evidence. The original ~/.dsh profile was not modified.
